To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coordinated application of coarse-grain transformations such as loop-invariant code-motion and CSE and fine-grain speculative code motions such as conditional speculation can significantly improve the performance and quality of synthesized designs with complex control flow.

High-level synthesis of designs with computationally complex control flows can be significantly accelerated by applying a coordinated set of source-level presynthesis transformations and scheduling transformations that include aggressive code motions such as conditional speculation and dynamic common sub-expression elimination.
a coordinated set of source level transformations and scheduling optimizations can be used to improve the quality of the design generated by behavioral synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of techniques for the automated generation of efficient hardware from behavioral specifications.
the application of aggressive code motions during scheduling to improve the quality of synthesis results for designs with complex control flow constructs.

developing new methodologies for high-level synthesis that are capable of exploiting coarse-grain parallelism and that are applicable to designs that have complex control flows and that are characterized by a high degree of data dependences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology we have developed has a significant impact on both the quality and efficiency of the synthesized designs.
the proposed methodology is a very powerful approach to the parallelization of complex designs with complex control-flow constructs.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of applying a coordinated set of parallelizing transformations in the context of a high-level synthesis environment, and have demonstrated that such an approach is useful for the synthesis of designs with control flow complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methodology can generate designs that can run at a frequency 2-3 times higher than the frequency obtained by a conventional high-level synthesis flow.

we have demonstrated that aggressive code restructuring transformations and scheduling techniques can be used effectively to optimize the results of high-level synthesis and to reduce the impact of control flows on the quality of synthesized designs.
our methodology can produce designs with a 2X to 4X speedup compared to designs produced by traditional behavioral synthesis approaches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of coarse-grain code transformations and fine-grain scheduling techniques can be effectively applied to optimize designs with complex control flow constructs.
the coordinated application of aggressive source level transformations and scheduling transformations can lead to significant performance gains for designs with complex control flow.
a coordinated set of aggressive source level and scheduling transformations, including dynamic CSE, can be used to generate high quality results for designs with complex control flow.
